No quota exemption is claimed; if fable is unavailable the dispatch stops and is re-recorded rather than silently dropped to a lower tier.

## Why the `Blocked-by: #9325` hold is released now, and what stays held

The card's hold has two distinct halves and only one of them has cleared. Recording both, because acting on the wrong one is how this lands in the wrong order:

**Cleared — the Settings swap is live.** Measured just now from two open PRs whose only relevant difference is the job's `name:`:

| PR | publishes `ESLint` | publishes `Lint & Repo Gates` | checks | `mergeable_state` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #9458 (head off pre-rename `main`) | ✅ | ❌ | 26/26 green | **`blocked`** |
| #9421 (the rename itself) | ❌ | ✅ | 22/22 green | **`clean`** |

A PR that is entirely green and still `blocked`, beside one that is green and `clean`, separates the required set from the check results with no access to Settings — which an agent seat does not have (HTTP 403, #6865). `Lint & Repo Gates` is required; `ESLint` is not. Step 3 of the sitting is therefore verified, and by a better instrument than the one planned: #9458 *is* the "open a PR after the swap and look at its required checks" test, already standing.

**Still held — #9421 has not merged.** `lint.yml` on `main` still names the job `ESLint`, so the checklist line this card fixes is still **literally correct today**. That is the "wrong in the other direction" window the card's ⚠️ names, and it is why this dispatch is for the implementation only:

> ⛔ **This card's PR must not merge before #9421 does.** Push it, open it, leave it. It will read `blocked` until its branch is updated onto a `main` that carries the rename — which is the correct state, not a defect to work around.

## Why the ordering broke, for the record

#9421 built green in the merge queue at 03:30:37Z and did not merge. It was batched behind #9458, which cannot satisfy the newly-required context until the rename is on `main` — so the group failed as a whole and both were ejected. `main` has not moved since 02:43Z for that reason. #9421 has been re-armed to enqueue alone.

The general consequence, which the reviewing seat should expect: **every open PR whose head predates the rename now reads `blocked`**, however green it is. The remedy is one branch update per PR after #9421 lands, not a change to any of them.

Under the sole recorded exit from the model-tiering ruling — **a measured quota exhaustion moves the card to opus, never lower** — this card is re-dispatched at **claude-opus-5**. The exemption is measured, not assumed: the tier was attempted first and refused by the provider, which is the condition the exemption names. This is the second time tonight (the first was #9415).

I said in the claim above that a fable-unavailable dispatch would be re-recorded rather than silently dropped. This comment is that record, and it stands as the card's authoritative `Container & model` line:

> **Container & model:** `claude-opus-5`, under the measured fable-quota exemption recorded here. Clause ① (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**`) still applies to the surface; it is the *seat* that moved, not the mandate.

## Compensating measure

Clause ① exists because a wrong edit to the PM lane's own protocol propagates into every later dispatch, and the tier is the safeguard. With the safeguard reduced, the PM seat substitutes a direct one: **I will review the resulting diff line by line against what the review checklist actually instructs the review seat to do**, rather than reviewing it against this card's description of that instruction. The card quotes line 37; the sweep may find more, and a paraphrase that reads well but changes what the seat is told to verify is the specific failure this substitutes for.

That review happens before the PR goes to a human. It does not replace the human merge — this surface is human-merge only under Prime Directive #14 regardless of tier.

## Two deviations from the dispatch prompt, both deliberate, neither silent

1. **The card's replacement phrasing was not used verbatim.** The prompt anticipated this and told me to distil rather than copy the `#9325` citation, and to stop and report if I concluded the citation was genuinely required. It is not required — the distilled form carries the operative content — so I implemented rather than stopped. What the prompt did not anticipate is that the phrasing it quotes as *already landed in `AGENTS.md` by #9421* is not what landed there: that PR hit the same gate and rewrote the sentence to carry the name history as prose plus the check-run-name mechanism. My wording mirrors what actually landed, not the card's proposal.

2. **The attribution footer uses the session-URL form**, not the bare `https://claude.ai/code` form the prompt spells out. The standing dev contract requires the session form because the bare form is stripped from a PR body on every later edit. The two conflict; the standing contract governs, and #9421's own body already uses the session form. Flagging rather than silently choosing.

## Left alone, on purpose

The PR is draft, unqueued, un-armed, and stays that way — human-merge only under Prime Directive #14, and it must land after #9421 regardless. `mergeable_state: blocked` was read once and left. No other PR, issue, assignee or label outside this card's own PR was touched.

## 1. The rename had already merged when I reported. My report said otherwise.

My report's summary says the PR "reads `mergeable_state: blocked`, which is correct until #9421 lands". That was written from the state at dispatch. Re-read after posting:

```
$ git fetch origin main && git rev-parse --short origin/main
81316864b
$ git show origin/main:.github/workflows/lint.yml | grep -n "name: Lint & Repo Gates"
39:    name: Lint & Repo Gates
```

#9421 landed as `81316864b` — the commit **immediately after** this branch's base `ad217b192`. So the sequencing condition the card names is **satisfied**, not pending, and the change is now correct rather than premature.

`mergeable_state: blocked` still reads the same, but for a different and benign reason: this branch's head predates the rename by one commit, so its own `lint.yml` still says `name: ESLint`. The standing remedy is one branch update, exactly as the claim comment above predicts for every open PR in this position. **I did not perform it** — the dispatch forbade chasing that state — so it is the merging human's call, and the PR remains draft, unarmed, unqueued.

PR #9490's body has been corrected accordingly: the "do not merge before #9421" section now records that the ordering is satisfied, with the measurement. No commit was made, so `0ec6cfc64` is still the head and the union readings in the report stand unchanged.

## 2. A second seat was dispatched onto this card and stopped correctly

`session_01Rn7aaamsR99FXRqLcpL99q` claimed this card at 04:28:42Z for branch `claude/issue-9420-review-checklist-lint-rename` — three seconds after PR #9490 was created at 04:28:39Z, which is why its "no open PR touches review-checklist.md" pre-check came up empty. That seat detected the collision, stopped before any edit, and reported `blocked` recommending this PR be adopted.

Recording it rather than acting on it: **the adjudication is the PM's, not mine.** I have not touched that seat's branch, its report, this card's assignee, or any label outside PR #9490's own. If the PM prefers option B in that seat's report, this PR closes cleanly — nothing depends on it.
